Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:87: In this same manner it also comes in the Tikkunim (26a, see also 9a), even more explicitly, explaining there that the donning of tefillin by a wicked person helps him to subdue his accusers, in these words: for the wicked, they are a binding for all their accusers. This shows that the special property of tefillin is to subdue the kelipot. And there is a second intention in the donning of tefillin, for one who is righteous or one who is intermediate, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:88: As for us, would that we were at the level of the intermediate ones — for Rabbah called himself intermediate (Berachot 61b), as we quoted at the end of chapter 6 of the Gate of Awe — it is good for us to wear tefillin all day, so that the kelipot may be subdued from us, and the straps be ropes for the horns of Samael, and so on. For even though our intention in donning tefillin may be directed above, to unify, as we shall explain, each person is affected by the spiritual power of the mitzvah according to the merit of his soul: if he is fully righteous, the Holy One, blessed be He, will be bound to him in love, and his soul bound with his soul, as explained in the passage; but even if he intends the aforementioned intention, the Holy One, blessed be He, will not be bound to him in love, but the mitzvah will only act upon him to subdue the kelipot.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:89: Now, because of the great greatness of the commandment of tefillin and its special properties, which we have explained and shall further explain, please God, one should arouse his heart and soul in love in fulfilling this mitzvah, so that his mind does not stray from them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:90: The matters that arouse love in this mitzvah, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Tikkunim (21b), in these words: and should you say that the Holy One, blessed be He, is not driven away with her [the Shechinah] — because of this the verse says, "As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man that wanders from his place" (Proverbs 27:8) — to guard her in exile from a foreign license; this is what is written, "I am the Lord, that is My Name, and My glory I will not give to another..." (Isaiah 42:8) — "to another" means to "another god," that is, Samael; "to the images" refers to the appointed [powers] over the seventy nations. Because of her, the Holy One, blessed be He, is "a king imprisoned in the tresses" (Song of Songs 7:6), and He is imprisoned with them in the hand-tefillin, in the knot of the hand — this is what is written, "bind your headdress (pe'ercha) upon you" (Ezekiel 24:17); and because He is imprisoned with them in exile, it is said of Him, "no prisoner frees himself from prison," and the Shechinah is His prison-house — because of His love for her He is imprisoned within her; and the mystery of the matter, "A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall lie between my breasts" (Song of Songs 1:13) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:91: Now, from the whole of his words, there is a lesson pertinent to our intention: when one considers that the Holy One, blessed be He, who is the King of the universe, is imprisoned together with a human being formed from a putrid drop, resting in the folds of the brain — and this is similar to how He confined His Shechinah between the poles of the Ark, even though the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him — therefore it is fitting that the thought of the soul dwelling within his brain should be attached to His love, blessed be He, resting in his brain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:92: And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach 175b) that the tefillin are witnesses testifying to a person that the Holy One, blessed be He, is attached to him, in these words: Rabbi Yehudah said, how many witnesses does the Holy One, blessed be He, make to testify concerning human beings! And all stand before Him in counsel and testimony. He rises in the morning and puts forth his feet to walk; witnesses stand before him proclaiming and saying, "He shall guard the feet of His pious ones" (I Samuel 2:9). He places the head-tefillah between his eyes; he must raise his head [and] see the holy supernal Name held fast and inscribed upon his head, and straps hanging on this side and that over his heart — behold, he has beheld the glory of his Master. He puts forth his hands, sees the other hand bound with the binding of the holy Name; he turns his hand and beholds the glory of his Master — so far his words, as pertains to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:93: Here it is made explicit that tefillin are witnesses testifying to a person so that he will not sin — for when he wishes to raise his eyes to see what is unfitting, or likewise with his hands, and he remembers that tefillin are on his head and his arm, he will fear the King who dwells with him. And it says, "[he must] see the supernal holy Name held fast and inscribed upon his head" — the word "held fast" means that the supernal holiness, literally, from above to below, is held fast upon him and does not separate from him — similar to what we said above, that regarding tefillin it is said, "And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" (Exodus 25:8).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:94: Let us return to the passage from the Tikkunim. It says at the end of that passage, "and the Shechinah is His prison-house, because of His love for her He is imprisoned within her." This is the aspect of the hand-tefillah, for the reality of the four portions in the hand-tefillah corresponds to Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, as Rashbi explains in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, beginning of 263a); it follows that this is the mystery of the male imprisoned in the house of the hand, and the house in which the portions are held, which is the Shechinah, is His prison-house, and for love of her He is imprisoned with her. Therefore the Shechinah says, "A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall lie between my breasts" — and this corresponds to the aspect of the hand-tefillah on the arm; this is [the meaning of] "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:95: This is similar to what she says, "Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm" (Song of Songs 8:6), which is explained in the Tikkunim (65b) to be said regarding the head- and hand-tefillin, in these words: "Set me as a seal upon your heart" — has anyone ever seen a seal upon a heart? Rather, it refers to the head-tefillin, whose straps hang down over the heart; and these are the head-tefillin, and the hand-tefillah, which is on the left, opposite the heart. This is [the meaning of] "as a seal upon your heart"; "as a seal upon your arm" is the hand-tefillah, in which are the markings of the holy Name — namely, Yod: "Sanctify to Me every firstborn"; Heh: "And it shall be when [the Lord] brings you"; Vav: "Hear, O Israel"; Heh: "And it shall be, if you shall hearken." And from that mark all the nations of the world tremble — this is what is written, "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you" (Deuteronomy 28:10), and so they have established: "the Name of the Lord" refers to the head-tefillin — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:96: Similar to this, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (Gate of Unity — Introduction), in explaining the passage "And you shall love," that all the things mentioned in that passage, such as "and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and you shall speak of them" (Deuteronomy 6:7), all arouse love; and it says afterward, "and you shall bind them for a sign...," and he writes, in these words: and afterward it moves from the duties of the limbs to the hand-tefillah and the head-tefillah and the mezuzah, and all of them cause one to remember the Creator and love Him with a whole heart, and finally he clothes it in the statute of the remembrance of the love of lovers, "Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm..." (Song of Songs 8:6), and it says, "A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall lie between my breasts" (Song of Songs 1:13) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:97: What the passage means by "because of her, the Holy One, blessed be He, is a king imprisoned in the tresses," and so on, can be understood from what is said in the Tikkunim (100b), whose wording we quoted in the Gate of Love, chapter 9 — that tefillin are called a "covering" to hide the Shechinah from the external forces. By this we can understand what they said in the Gemara (Shabbat 49a), that tefillin are called "wings of a dove," concerning Elisha "the man of wings"; and it is written, "the wings of a dove covered with silver" (Psalms 68:14), which is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 102a) to mean that the thread of Chesed, which is silver, covers and conceals the Shechinah and the neshamah from the prosecutors — and this is a great special property that tefillin have beyond all else that has been discussed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:98: And so it is further explained in the Tikkunim (end of 143a), in these words: there are sins for which souls are judged with harsh judgments, but let the mitzvah come — she who is the Matronita, such as the commandment of tefillin — and shield over it and spread her wings over it, and the accuser has no permission to draw near there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:99: Among the things that arouse love in this mitzvah is when one considers that the tefillin we wear, though they are tefillin of leather, in their supernal place are tefillin of light. This is the mystery explained in the Tikkunim (84a) and in the Zohar, that the Holy One, blessed be He, wears tefillin — meaning that Tiferet is crowned with the supernal lights, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan 262b). Had Adam not sinned, or had Israel not sinned with the Golden Calf, they would have been refined like angels, and would have merited tefillin of light; but after the sin, Israel merited only tefillin of leather — meaning the constriction of the supernal lights into the world of Metatron, in which is the mystery of exile on the weekdays, and in which are tefillin of leather, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan 264b): for concerning tefillin it is said, "And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin (or)" (Genesis 3:21), in these words: Rabbi Abba sent [word] to Rabbi Shimon, saying to him, this that they established regarding the tefillin of the Master of the universe, that they are the holy of holies, [and] the leather of the tefillin and the straps are called "holiness" — from where do we support this? He sent [word] to him, "And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin" — precisely; and so Rav Hamnuna the Elder established it, and these are [the tefillin] of the head and the arm, YHVH-Kaf-Heh, and this has already been established — so far his words. It is known that this verse, "And the Lord God made," is a rectification for after the sin of Adam; and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (10b), in these words: at first, "garments of light" (ohr, spelled with an aleph), by which his heel dimmed the orb of the sun, this being "the Creator of the lights of fire" (borei me'orei ha'esh); after they sinned, "And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin" (or, spelled with an ayin) — so far his words, as pertains to us; and this wording is understood in light of what we have already introduced.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:100: And in the Tikkunim (113, second part) they explain the matter explicitly, in these words: after Adam, below, contemplated repentance, the garment returned to the brain, which is the skull of the tefillin, and the brain, which is Chochmah, joined with Imma; immediately, "And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin, and clothed them" — these are the tefillin, which are made of leather (skin). At that time repentance arose, which is Imma, the skull of the tefillin, together with Adam, to shield him and to cover him because he was naked — in the manner that she covers the supernal brain; and so, whoever dons tefillin, it is as though he covers the supernal brain — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:101: When a person contemplates what we have explained, his heart will be enkindled with love for the Creator, who had mercy upon him and constricted the supernal lights for him, clothed in tefillin of leather. This is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, mentioned in Song of Songs regarding the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel, "a king imprisoned in the tresses" (Song of Songs 7:6), which refers to the head-tefillin, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:102: When a person dons tefillin he is a complete person, resembling his Maker, as is explained in the Tikkunim (83b), in these words: "And God created man in His image, in the image of God He created him" (Genesis 1:27) — here is the commandment of tefillin. Come and see, whoever dons tefillin upon his head and his arm — a voice ascends every day to all the living creatures, chariots, wheels, seraphim, and angels appointed over prayers: "Give honor to the image of the King" — that is, to whoever dons tefillin, concerning whom it is said, "And God created man in His image, in the image of God He created him." "In His image" — the head-tefillin, in the manner of the tefillin of the Master of the universe, which are the supernal Shechinah, tefillin upon the head, which is the middle pillar, comprising the first three sefirot, and the middle pillar comprising six sefirot; and the supernal Imma, tefillin upon His head, is what the Holy One, blessed be He, dons every day. The hand-tefillah — this is the lower Shechinah, who is bound to Him, of whom it is said, "and his soul is bound up with his soul" (Genesis 44:30), both of them in one unification, in one binding. The strap wound around the left finger is her betrothal, for it is a ring wound around her finger, by which she is bound to Him and He to her — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:103: This passage makes clear the greatness of one who dons tefillin — that he resembles his Maker — and it partially explains the intent of tefillin, which will be further explained, please God. Incidentally, it is made clear that the strap we wind around the finger is the betrothal ring that the male gives to her; and from this my teacher, peace be upon him, used to say that it is not proper to wind the strap around the finger until one has already donned the head-tefillah, which is the mystery of the male — for if the male has not yet come, from where would the betrothal be? This is likewise the practice of most of Israel, and it is not fitting to change the custom. And my teacher, peace be upon him, likewise used to say that this winding upon the finger must be done while standing, for the male who betroths the woman betroths her while standing, since the betrothal is from the world of the male, and his way is standing. And the windings must be three, as explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas 228b), whose wording we quoted above regarding the number of sections in the tzitzit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:104: Further, regarding the greatness of one who dons tefillin and tzitzit, it is elaborated in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim 81a), where it says that whoever dons tefillin and tzitzit is one, resembling his Maker, and since he resembles his Maker, there is an affinity and closeness for the Holy One, blessed be He, to rest upon him; but if he does not resemble his Maker, what affinity does the Holy One, blessed be He, have with him? In these words: "You shall be holy" (Leviticus 19:2). Rabbi Abba opened, "And who is like Your people Israel, a unique nation on the earth" (I Chronicles 17:21). Come and see, of all the nations of the world the Holy One, blessed be He, chose none but Israel alone, and made them one nation, and called them one nation by His own name, and crowned them with many crowns, with many commandments, to be crowned with them; and therefore the head-tefillin and the arm-tefillin, for a person to be crowned with them in the manner above, and to become one, complete in everything. And at that hour that a person is crowned with them and sanctified with them, he becomes complete and is called "one" — for "one" is called such only when complete, and one who is blemished is not called "one." Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "one" in the completeness of everything, in the completeness of the Patriarchs, in the completeness of the Community of Israel; and therefore Israel below are called "one" — for when a person dons tefillin and is covered with the covering of the mitzvah [of tzitzit], then he is crowned with holy crowns in the manner above, and is called "one." Therefore, let "one" come and occupy itself with "one" — the Holy One, blessed be He, who is one, will occupy Himself with the one, for a king occupies himself only with what is fitting for him; therefore it is written, "But He is one, and who can turn Him?" (Job 23:13) — the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells and is found only in "one." "In one" — it should have said simply "one"; rather, it means, in whoever has arranged himself with supernal holiness so as to become one — then He dwells in "one," and not in another place. And when is a person called "one"? At the hour he is sanctified with the supernal crowns — so far his words. This makes it explicit that the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells and is found only in "one" — namely, after a person is arranged with tzitzit and tefillin, for then he is one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:105: If so, at the time a person is occupied with Torah or prayer, when he wants the Holy One, blessed be He, to rest with him, if he is blemished and lacking the vessel and ornaments of holiness, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest upon him, as they said above, "and whoever is blemished is not called one." It is possible that this is [the meaning of] the blessing over tefillin, saying "who has sanctified us with His commandments," according to the plain sense — for since a person wishes to be attached to Him, blessed be He, he must first sanctify himself with His commandments, and by this there is preparation for all supernal holiness to rest [upon him].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:106: Regarding the intention for donning tefillin, I shall quote what is found in the Zohar and the Tikkunim, scattered in various places, gathering them here — and let the understanding reader understand. They said, of blessed memory (Parashat Metzora 55a): whoever dons tefillin, when he puts on the hand-tefillah, should extend his left arm to receive the Community of Israel [with it], and bind the knot with the right, in order to embrace her — to fulfill what is written, "his left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me" (Song of Songs 2:6) — so that a person may appear in the manner above and be crowned with everything; and then a person is complete in supernal holiness, and the Holy One, blessed be He, calls him "Israel, in whom I take glory" (Isaiah 49:3) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:107: And when he dons the head-tefillah, and so on, he should stand, [corresponding] to the world of the male; and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Chayei Sarah 132b) that all matters that are from the world of the male require standing upright — see also there (Parashat Terumah, beginning of 133a), regarding sanctity said standing or sitting. And concerning this they said in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 42a): Rabbi Yishmael said, had Israel merited nothing but to receive the presence of their Father in Heaven once every month, it would suffice them. Abaye said, therefore one must say it standing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:108: When he dons the hand-tefillah, he should join the knot of the Yod with the box (bayit). This is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas 236b), in these words: this Yod must not depart at all from within the hand-tefillah, so that it not create a separation, and all her joy is in this — the Yod is in the male and not in the female, and therefore she draws close to Him; and whoever distances himself from this place distances himself from the delight of the World to Come with the male — he is Tzaddik (righteous, masculine) and she is Tzedek (righteous, feminine) without a Yod; he is Ish (man) and she is Ishah (woman) without a Yod — and therefore his joy is to draw near to her and delight with her. Whoever distances this delight, they will distance him from the supernal delight; concerning this it is written, "For those who honor Me I will honor..." (I Samuel 2:30) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:109: In the intention for the hand-tefillah and the head-tefillah, one should intend in the hand-tefillah that the four portions are the Name YHVH, as explained above — "Sanctify" is Yod; "And it shall be when [the Lord] brings you" is Heh; "Hear, O Israel" is Vav; "And it shall be, if you shall hearken" is Heh; and the box is the Name Adonai. And in the head-tefillah, the four portions are the Name YHVH in four boxes, [each of] which is the Name Ehyeh. So it is explained in the Tikkunim (9a), in these words: "Then you shall call, and YHVH shall answer" (Isaiah 58:9) — YHVH is in the four boxes of the head-tefillin, which are the four letters Ehyeh; "and YHVH shall answer" — YHVH is in the four boxes of the hand-tefillah, which are [the Name] Adonai. And should you say, are they not in the hand as a single box, and so on? — so far his words, as pertains to us. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:110: Further, in the Tikkunim (144b), in these words: "Your head upon you is like Carmel" (Song of Songs 7:6) — this is the head-tefillin, and the straps hanging from here are like the tendrils that are like Carmel, hanging from the vine. "And the locks of your head like purple (argaman)" — this is the hand-tefillah; what had been a "locks" (dal, poor/impoverished) in poor exile — this is what is written, "a prayer of the afflicted, when he faints" (Psalms 102:1) — shall become a garment like argaman, which is the mystery of Uriel, Raphael, Gabriel, Michael, Nuriel. "A king imprisoned in the tresses" — this is the Holy One, blessed be He, YHVH, who is imprisoned in her four boxes, which are Adonai, the four folds of the brain, that he be imprisoned in the tresses in this manner — YAKDONKY (a combined form), "for Your Name is in you and Your Name is in you" — and this is the mystery of "amen" from "argaman" — so far his words. And at the end of the passage, regarding "a king imprisoned in the tresses," it agrees with the preceding passage; and the general principle is that the hand-tefillah is the "head" of the female, and the folds of the brain within her are the Name Adonai. And the strap of the hand is what it calls "your locks" — an allusion to the hair of her head, up to "argaman," as explained in the passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:111: Further, in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, beginning of 263a), regarding the intention for donning tefillin, in these words: Rabbi Yitzchak taught, the supernal holy chariot is the four boxes of the tefillin that Vav dons, as has been stated; the other holy chariot is the other four, comprised in one, that the final Heh dons, as has been established. And further, it is written there (end of 264a, in a gloss) — and this is the gloss's wording — the head-tefillin are Chochmah, Binah, Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet of the one wearing it; and the arm-tefillin are Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malchut of the one wearing it — so far his words. And let it not seem difficult that the Tikkunim explain that the four portions are the Name YHVH, [while here it lists different sefirot], for the intent is that Vav leans toward the right, Chesed, and Heh leans toward the left, Gevurah — so my teacher, peace be upon him, explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:112: Before putting on the tefillin, one should say, "I am putting on tefillin to fulfill the commandment of my Creator, 'and you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes'" — the four portions in the hand [-tefillah], and so on — intending that they correspond to the Name YHVH clothed within the Name Adonai, which is the box, and the twenty-one mentions within it corresponding to the Name Ehyeh. And in the head [-tefillin] are the four portions of YHVH, and the four boxes of Ehyeh, and further the Name Ehyeh within it corresponding to the twenty-one mentions; and one should intend to subdue the maidservant beneath her mistress, and so on, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:113: Regarding the intention of the mentions [of the Divine Name] within the tefillin, which are [the Name] Ehyeh — twenty-one in the hand and twenty-one in the head, which are forty-two — it is explained in the Tikkunim (3a), in these words: "Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh" within the tefillin, in the twenty-one mentions of the head-tefillin and in the twenty-one mentions of the hand-tefillah; and this is the supernal Imma — we call it the tefillin of the Master of the universe. Tefillin upon the head of the middle pillar, "Hear, O Israel" — the supernal Imma covers Him with her wings, which are the straps of the tefillin — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:114: According to the plain sense, one should intend the actual portions written within the tefillin, and by this the heart is aroused to love. In the first two portions, "Sanctify" and "And it shall be when [the Lord] brings you," corresponding to Yod-Heh, one should think of what is written in them — namely, the matter of the Exodus from Egypt, which indicates the intensity of the Holy One, blessed be He's love — that He Himself went to bring them out from there and slew their firstborn. And one might give a parable: a king whose son is captive; the king himself goes, for love of his son, and forcibly brings him out, and wages war with his captor. So the Holy One, blessed be He, in His own glory and by Himself — not an angel and not a seraph — killed their firstborn and brought them out, as it says, "and the Lord smote every firstborn" (Exodus 12:29); and this is what Moses warns Israel, "Remember this day on which you came out of Egypt... for with a strong hand the Lord brought you out from this place..." (Exodus 13:3). And the word "Remember" is in the infinitive [imperative], for we are forever obligated to remember this matter, so that we remember His love in our hearts and serve Him like a son who loves his father because of the good He did for him; and the verse calls us "sons," as it says, "My son, My firstborn, Israel" (Exodus 4:22) — and the intent is regarding the holy neshamah that flowed to us from the place of holiness, from where the firstborn is holy; therefore it says, "Sanctify to Me every firstborn" (Exodus 13:2); and because of this we are obligated to sanctify ourselves so that we may be attached to Him. This matter is written in the second portion, and there the killing of the firstborn is explained further, in saying, "and the Lord slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of man to the firstborn of beast" (Exodus 13:15); and in these two portions He informs us of the matter of [divine] providence and power, for He rearranged the arrangements of the heavens and broke the iron bolts, as explained in the Zohar; and it is likewise written, "but you the Lord has taken and brought forth out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be for Him a people of inheritance" (Deuteronomy 4:20).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:115: In the two portions "Shema" and "And it shall be, if you shall hearken," it reminds us of the unity of God — that is, YHVH is one, above and below, and in the four directions of the world, which we saw at the standing at Mount Sinai, as explained in chapter 1 of the Gate of Awe; and afterward it warns us regarding love, that we should make signs for the reality of this love, so that His love not depart from our hearts: "and these words which I command you today" — regarding the matter of love and unity — "shall be upon your heart. And you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall speak of them when you sit in your house...," "and you shall bind them for a sign," so that we remember the love and the unity. This matter is written in the portion "And it shall be, if you shall hearken," "to love...," except that it warns us that if our heart is enticed after the evil inclination, which is "other gods," "then the Lord's anger will be kindled..."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:116: Regarding the head-straps, and the knot of the head-tefillin and the hand-tefillah, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas 236b), in these words: two straps go out on this side and that, being the two thighs of this Aleph and Chet, upon which the true prophets take hold — for from above go out two arms, right and left, and the Dalet is bound to them; afterward the thighs spread out below; once she is bound above as is fitting, she descends below to be bound to her hosts; when she is bound she takes hold of the ends of the thighs, and the mark of the Yod of the supernal holy Covenant from above; then she is bound in unification — so far his words, as pertains to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:117: Further, regarding the hand-strap, it is said in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, beginning of 263a), in these words: and therefore, from this one strap hangs down below, for from her the lower ones hang and are nourished; therefore she is called "a sign," as it says, "this is the sign of the covenant" (Genesis 9:12), and it is written, "for a sign upon your hand" [read as] Yod-Kaf-Heh, and this has already been established.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:118: Further, regarding the mystery of the straps, they explain, of blessed memory (Tikkunei Zohar 9b): three straps — Netzach, Hod, Yesod. Yesod is the strap that binds Vav with Heh, "for the earth and everything in the heavens and on the earth" — that holds fast the heavens and the earth. Two straps, Netzach and Hod, which hold fast to the supernal Heh; and "the horns are high, one higher than the other" — likewise the two straps, one long and one short. The short goes to the chest, the long to the navel. And the spreading of the supernal Heh to Hod, in the letter Yod — this is the knot of the head-tefillin, that the supernal Heh ascends to fifty, five times ten in the letter Yod — this is from the Heh-Yod of "Elohim," five times Heh in the letter Yod, fifty in five sefirot. Yesod, "All" (kol), takes hold of them all and inherits them all for the bride — this is "kalah" (bride/completed). In the letter Heh below, one horn — and the mystery of this matter, our Rabbis established, [regarding] the ox that Adam offered had one horn on its forehead, as it is said, "[this shall please the Lord] more than a bull or bullock that has horns and hooves" (Psalms 69:32), [reading] "keren" (horn) without a Yod [i.e., singular] — and this is the strap of the hand-tefillah of the Master of the universe — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:119: Regarding the mystery of the Shins on the tefillin, it says in the Tikkunim (9a), in these words: the Shin of the tefillin is a law given to Moses at Sinai — a Shin with three heads, a Shin with four heads, corresponding to the seven maidens fit to be given to her from the king's house, which are in the morning: two before her and one after her; and in the evening: two before her and two after her (Berachot 1:4, mishnah) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:120: Further, there (26a), in these words: the Shin of the tefillin — this is the supernal Imma, of whom it is said, "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you" (Deuteronomy 28:10). "Shin" numerically equals, with its letters, 360 (Shin-Samech); the fourth Heh is dim, [reducing it to] 365. And the two hundred forty-eight commandments comprised within the two hundred forty-eight words of the Shema, in its four portions, total 613 — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:121: Thus far we have gathered what pertains from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, to the intention of donning tzitzit and tefillin. When a person intends all of this, and secludes himself by day and occupies himself with Torah in awe and love, with intention as stated, and intends the mystery of the Name Yod-Kei Vav-Kei, which is the Name of thought as explained at the beginning of the chapter, he will certainly draw holiness to sanctify his thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:122: It is good that after donning the tallit and tefillin one should intend the Name Yod-Kai Vav-Kai, which is explained in the Tikkunim (9b) to contain the mystery of tefillin and tzitzit, in these words: and there is a point in another mystery, in the manner of "YHVH reigns, YHVH has reigned, YHVH shall reign" — whose Names from above have their vowel points written beneath them, hanging by four Names from each and every Name; and concerning them it is said, "and one called to another" (Isaiah 6:3), corresponding to the twelve faces of the three living creatures; "to another," twelve wings of the three living creatures; and above them all, the face of a man. And tefillin is the face of a man; tzitzit is the faces of the [other] living creatures and the wings of the living creatures. Our Rabbis established there, the Name of Twelve — whoever knows it and is careful with it, all his prayers are accepted; its source is Yod-Kai Vav-Kai — every Yod is His faces, YHVH; Aleph — "and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man" (Ezekiel 1:10) — here, in this Name, is the mystery of tefillin and tzitzit — so far his words. This Name is explained in the Tikkunim, and likewise in other places in the Tikkunim, as being the brain-thought within Chochmah, which is within Keter, and it benefits the holiness of thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:123: The place where it is explicitly explained (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 100a), I saw fit to quote here, in these words: and this is your card — "Zarka Makaf Shofar Holech Segulta" [names of cantillation marks] — for this stone ascends from your mouth to the place of which it is said, "that which is too wondrous for you, do not seek out, and that which is hidden from you, do not investigate" (based on Chagigah 13a); and this is the Name of the supernal Keter, which is the primordial Chochmah — for "Chochmah" thus numerically equals the holy Name together with the ten letters included in it, which are Yod-Kai Vav-Kai — so far his words. And further on: because there descend upon her the ten segulot (properties) of the Name of the Keter, which are Yod-Kai Vav-Kai, which are sefirot full of segulot that surround the supernal Keter of the King and the Matronita; and this is the supernal Keter, of which it is said, on the day of Shabbat, in the Kedushah, "A crown they shall give You, O Lord our God..." — so far his words, as pertains to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 6:124: There are still other aspects to the holiness of thought, and we saw fit to explain them in a chapter of their own, in order to give some breathing room between chapters.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:1: We have already explained, at the beginning of the preceding chapter, that the brain and the heart are the two primary limbs upon which thought depends, and we have explained the matter of the holiness of thought that depends upon the brain, according to what is found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:2: Further, we find in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (63a), regarding the matter of blessing, holiness, and unity, that he explains they are lion, ox, eagle, which are Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet; and three limbs in a person correspond to them: brain, heart, lung; and three accusers correspond to them: spleen, gall bladder, liver. And upon this chariot rests the face of the supernal Man, which is the mystery of the supernal Thought — and this is a good thought, as explained at the beginning of the preceding chapter; and there is an evil thought, which is [called] "a base man, a man of iniquity" (Proverbs 6:12), "man is like a breath" (Psalms 144:4). From this you can see how great a blemish is caused by one who thinks strange thoughts, that he is uprooted from a supernal place to the place of impurity, which is "a base man," and so on (Proverbs, ibid.).
